It should’ve been called Golden Arrows or Safed Sagar ;Chapter Toni.

Safed Sagar was a much bigger operation:

7,631 IAF sorties, of which 3,427 were transport sorties, the backbone of the logistics effort.

2,474 helicopter sorties, involving everything from troop/logistics support to casualty evacuation and high-risk missions.

1,730 fighter sorties and within the fast-jet missions, Mirage 2000 alone accounted for 514 sorties, over 30% of the documented squadron total. No. 7 Squadron alone flew 240 strike missions and dropped ~55 tonnes of ordnance.

And I would’ve loved to see the series acknowledge Squadron Leader Rajiv Pundir, Flight Lieutenant Muhilan, Sergeant RK Sahu and Sergeant PVNR Prasad (the four air warriors of the Mi-17 crew who made the supreme sacrifice.

The fighters were only one part of a much larger air campaign.

No. 9 Squadron’s MiG-27MLs played a significant role. Jaguars flew too. The Canberra took a hit while conducting reconnaissance.

And perhaps the quietest but most consequential player was the MiG-29, the air-superiority shield that helped ensure Pakistani F-16s stayed on the other side of the BVR equation.

There were two moments in the series that gave me strong Sherdil vibes.
